HEADQUARTERS CRIME BRANCH
F.M. 2
G. 15000-1-38 MISCELLANEOUS FILE SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
No 177/38
Date 20 ... 11 ... 1939

D. C. (Special Branch).

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
R. No. S. B. D. Station 1299/38
Date January 11, 1939

REPORT

Subject ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE.

Made by D. S. Bradley Forwarded by D. I. Glover

Sir,

Since the arrest of the 5 suspects for the Japanese Military Police, detectives have made intensive enquiries regarding their activities and no proof has been found regarding the allegations made against them that they had come to Shanghai to buy firearms.

When they were arrested on 29-12-38 no evidence was found against them, and since that time the Japanese Military Police have not come forward with any proof that they were here to buy firearms or that the rice brought by them from Kiangyin was stolen.

The receipt (attached) which was found in the possession of the 3rd accused, seems proof enough that the rice brought to Shanghai by him for sale was obtained in a legal manner from the Yah Woo Koong Chi (協和公記) Foodstuff Hong, Loh Mai Jiao (陸家橋).

All 5 of the accused appear to be men of honest character who have only come to Shanghai to negotiate a perfectly harmless rice deal and the only proof submitted by the Japanese Military Police to the contrary is the statement of a Chinese informer in the pay of the Japanese Military Police who alleges that they came to Shanghai to purchase firearms, and he cannot substantiate his allegations.

If the 5 suspects really came to Shanghai to buy firearms and the Japanese Military Police knew so much about their activities, there is no known reason why they should be arrested before they had bought the firearms and then, not only would there be evidence against them, but it would have allowed

（左侧边缘手写批注及印章：）
S.
B.
（印：MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 12.1.39）

第 177/38 号
日期 1939 年 11 月 20 日

D. C. (特务科)。

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特务科登记处
R. No. S. B. D. 分局 1299/38
日期 1939 年 1 月 11 日

报告

事由：协助日本宪兵队。

呈报人：D. S. Bradley 转呈人：D. I. Glover

先生，

自从为日本宪兵队逮捕了 5 名嫌疑人以来，侦探们对其活动进行了密集调查，但并未发现任何证据能证实针对他们的指控，即他们来上海是为了购买枪支。

在 1938 年 12 月 29 日逮捕他们时，并未发现针对他们的证据，自那时起，日本宪兵队也未提供任何证据证明他们来此是为了购买枪支，或者证明他们从江苏（Kiangsu）江阴带来的大米是偷窃所得。

在第 3 名被告身上发现的收据（附后）似乎足以证明，他带到上海出售的大米是从陆家桥（Loh Mai Jiao）的协和公记（Yah Woo Koong Chi）食品行合法获得的。

这 5 名被告似乎都是品行端正的人，他们来上海只是为了洽谈一笔完全无害的大米交易，而日本宪兵队提出的相反证据仅是一名受雇于日本宪兵队的中国线人的陈述，该线人称他们来上海是为了购买枪支，但他无法证实其指控。

如果这 5 名嫌疑人真的是来上海购买枪支，且日本宪兵队对他们的活动如此了解，那么没有理由在他们尚未购买枪支之前就将其逮捕，因为这样做不仅会有针对他们的证据，而且还将允许

（左侧边缘手写批注及印章：）
S.
B.
（印：MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 1939.1.12）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of SUNG TAI KAU ( **〔此处转录不清〕** ), 36, M/Merchant,
native of Kiangying taken by No. J.D.S. 172,
at C. 1 on the 29.12.38 and interpreted by Yao.

I am a cloth merchant at Loh Ka Jiao, Tsoh Daung Village,
Kiangying. I am now living at Room 52, Hung Zieng Lodging House,
Avenue Road.

I am a native of Loh Ka Jiao, Tsoh Daung Village, Kiang-
ying, where my family, brother, sister and an aged mother are
now living. There we have 43 mows of land and six small houses,
and trading in native cloth is my profession.

On 22.12.38 I came to Shanghai with the other four men
all in custody, taking with us 94 piculs of rice per s/s Han Wo.
On arrival, the rice were moved to 260 Shanhaikwan Road, the
Yung Hsing Rice Hong, to whom we intended to sell. However,
owing to their offer being too low, the cargo of rice was then
stored in that hong, awaiting a better chance for sale, and all
of us engaged Room 52 in Hung Zieng Lodging House as temporal
quarters.

As we were waiting for the chance to sell our rice at a
better price, we were arrested.

I had never been in the employ of any government organs,
military, police etc.

Signed, finger printed : SUNG TAI KAU.

S. G.M.-P. 2a

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警方调查报告。

以下是 SUNG TAI KAU（ **〔此处转录不清〕** ），36 岁，男/商人，
江苏江阴籍，由编号 J.D.S. 172 的警员
于 1938 年 12 月 29 日在 C. 1 处录取，由 Yao 翻译。

我是江苏江阴曹荡村陆家桥（Loh Ka Jiao）的一名布商。我现在住在爱文义路（Avenue Road）鸿祥旅馆（Hung Zieng Lodging House）52 号房间。

我是江苏江阴曹荡村陆家桥人，我的家人、兄弟、姐妹和年迈的母亲现在都住在那里。我们在那里有 43 亩土地和六间小房子，经营土布是我的职业。

1938 年 12 月 22 日，我与另外四名目前均在押的男子一同乘“汉沃”号（Han Wo）轮船来到上海，随身携带 94 担大米。抵达后，大米被运往山海关路 260 号的永兴米行（Yung Hsing Rice Hong），我们打算将米卖给他们。然而，由于他们出价太低，这批大米随后储存在该行内，等待更好的销售机会，我们所有人则租用鸿祥旅馆 52 号房间作为临时住所。

正当我们等待以更好价格出售大米的机会时，我们被捕了。

我从未在任何政府机关、军队、警察等部门任职。

签名并按指印：SUNG TAI KAU。

The following is the statement of TSANG ZAU LIH ( **〔此处转录不清〕** ), 25, M/Farmer,
native of Kiengying taken by me C.D.S.172
at C.1 on the 29.12.38 and interpreted by Yao.

I am a farmer in Loh Ka Jiao, Tsoh Daung Village, Kiang-
ying, where I have 41 mows of land and three flats to accomodate
my parents, brother, wife and children. We live on the rice
raised from our own fields. I am at present living in Room 52,
Hung Zirng Lodging House, Avenue Road.

On 22.12.38 I obtained 43 sacks of rice from my native
place, loaded them on board a British s/s "Han Woo" and came to
Shanghai with intentions to sell. On arrival, the cargo of rice
was moved to the Yung Hsing Rice Hong, 260 Shanhaikwen Road,
where I demanded $500.00 for it. However, before the rice hong
had paid me the price for the cargo, I was arrested together with
four friends at room 52 of that lodging house.

I have never held any government positions.

This is the truth.

Signed, finger printed by : TSANG ZAU LAI.

===
警方调查报告。
===

以下是 TSANG ZAU LIH（ **〔此处转录不清〕** ），25 岁，男/农民，
江苏江阴籍，由我 C.D.S.172
于 1938 年 12 月 29 日在 C.1 处录取，由 Yao 翻译。

我是江苏江阴曹荡村陆家桥（Loh Ka Jiao）的一名农民，在那里我有 41 亩土地和三间平房，供我的父母、兄弟、妻子和孩子居住。我们靠自家田地出产的大米为生。我目前住在爱文义路（Avenue Road）鸿祥旅馆（Hung Zirng Lodging House）52 号房间。

1938 年 12 月 22 日，我从家乡弄到 43 袋大米，装上英国轮船“汉沃”号（Han Woo），打算来上海出售。抵达后，这批大米被运往山海关路 260 号的永兴米行，我索要价金 500.00 美元。然而，在米行支付货款之前，我与四位朋友在那家旅馆的 52 号房间一同被捕。

我从未担任过任何政府职务。

此为实情。

签名并按指印：TSANG ZAU LAI。

Ziang Lodging House, Avenue Road.
On 22.12.38, my friend Sung Tai Kau and myself both put
up a capital and bought 94 sacks of rice, which was loaded on
board a British s/s "Hen Woo" and transported to Shanghai. On
arrival, the cargo of rice was moved to the Yung Hsing Rice Hong,
260 Shanhaikwan Road, to whom we negotiated for sale. However,
as the price offered was too low, we stored the rice there and
awaited for a better chance to sell it. In Room 52 of that lodging
house, we were arrested.
I have never worked in the police, military or any gov't
positions.
This is the truth.

Sd. LI EU OEN ZAU.

以下是 LOH OEN ZAU（ 〔此处转录不清〕 ），35 岁，男/农民，
江苏江阴籍，由 C.D.S. 172 先生
于 1938 年 12 月 28 日在 C.1 处录取，由 Yao 翻译。

我是江苏江阴曹荡村陆家桥（Loh Ka Jiao）的一名农民，在那里我有 5 亩土地，用以供养我的母亲、阿姨和姐妹。在上海，我住在爱文义路（Avenue Road）鸿祥旅馆（Hung Ziang Lodging House）52 号房间。
1938 年 12 月 22 日，我的朋友 Sung Tai Kau 和我共同出资购买了 94 袋大米，装上英国轮船“汉沃”号（Hen Woo）运往上海。抵达后，这批大米被运往山海关路 260 号的永兴米行，我们与其洽谈出售事宜。然而，由于出价太低，我们将大米储存在那里，等待更好的销售机会。在那家旅馆的 52 号房间，我们被捕了。
我从未在警察、军队或任何政府部门工作过。
此为实情。

签名：LI EU OEN ZAU。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of TONG CHING FONG (〔此处转录不清〕), 34, M/Farmer,
native of Kiangying taken by me C.D.3.172
at C. 1 on the 29/12/38 and interpreted by Yao

I am a farmer at Loh Ka Jiao, Tsoh Daung Village, Kiang-
Ying. I am now living in Room 52 Hung Zi ng Lodging House,
venue Road.
I was brought up in Kiangying, where I have 8 mows of
land, and an aged mother, wife and children to take care of.
I lived on the proceeds of the field.
On 22.12.38, I and four friends came to Shanghai per s/s
Han Au to sell some 50 sacks of rice. On arrival, I stored
my rice in the Yui Zung Godown, Kiukiang Road, awaiting a
chance to sell it at a better price. All of us lived in Room
No.52 of that lodging House, until several days ago, when we
were arrested.
I had never served in any government organisations,
police, military et al. This is the truth.

Signed : TONG CHING FONG.

我是江苏江阴曹荡村陆家桥（Loh Ka Jiao）的一名农民。我现在住在爱文义路（venue Road）鸿祥旅馆（Hung Zi ng Lodging House）52 号房间。
我在江苏江阴长大，在那里我有 8 亩土地，以及需要照顾的年迈母亲、妻子和孩子。
我靠田地产出生活。
1938 年 12 月 22 日，我和四位朋友乘“汉奥”号（Han Au）轮船来上海出售约 50 袋大米。抵达后，我将大米存放在九江路（Kiukiang Road）的裕丰仓库（Yui Zung Godown），等待以更好价格出售的机会。我们都住在那家旅馆的 52 号房间，直到几天前被捕。
我从未在任何政府组织、警察、军队等机构服役。此为实情。

TSANG AH KYUNG ( **〔此处转录不清〕** ), 33, M/Farmer,
The following is the statement of ____________________ C.D.S. 172,
native of _______ Kiangying, _______ taken by me ____________________ Yao.
at _______ C.1 _______ on the ___ 29.12.38 ___ and interpreted by ____________________

I am a farmer at Loh Ka Jiao, Tsoh Daung Village,
Kiangying, where I have in possession 3 mows of land and
a wooden sail boat to live on. (The No. of the sail boat,
allotted by the former City Government, No.57129). There
are five persons in my family, my parents, wife and two
children, who all assist me either as a farmer or as a
boatman.

On 22.12.38 I purchased 66 piculs of rice and came
to Shanghai with 4 friends per s/s Han Wu. On arrival, I
moved my cargo of rice to the Yung Hsing Rice Hong, 260 Shan-
haikwan Road, where .. demanded $600.00 for same. I was paid
$500.00 first, the balance to be cleared later. This $600
was handed to my friend Wong Dau Tuh on 28.12.38 who was sending
same to my home in Kiangying.

In Shanghai, I and the four friends all put up in
Room 52, Hung Ziang Lodging House, Avenue Road. We intended
to depart for Kiangying as soon as all the transactions of
the other friends had concluded. But soon we were arrested.
This is the truth.

I had never been working in a gov't position, police
military etc.

Signed : TSANG AH KYUNG.

以下是 ___ 的陈述，由我 ___ 录取，___ 翻译。
籍贯 _______ 江苏江阴，_______ 于 ___ 1938 年 12 月 29 日 ___ 在 _______ C.1 _______ 处录取，由 ___ Yao ___ 翻译

我是江苏江阴曹荡村陆家桥（Loh Ka Jiao）的一名农民，在那里我拥有 3 亩土地和一艘赖以生存的木帆船。（帆船号码由前市政府分配，编号 57129）。我家有五口人，包括我的父母、妻子和两个孩子，他们都协助我从事农耕或船夫工作。

1938 年 12 月 22 日，我购买了 66 担大米，与 4 位朋友乘“汉武”号（Han Wu）轮船来到上海。抵达后，我将这批大米运往山海关路 260 号的永兴米行，并为此索要 600.00 美元。我先收到了 500.00 美元，余款稍后结清。这 600 美元于 1938 年 12 月 28 日交给我的朋友 Wong Dau Tuh，由他寄回我在江苏江阴的家中。

在上海，我和四位朋友都住在爱文义路（Avenue Road）鸿祥旅馆（Hung Ziang Lodging House）52 号房间。我们打算在其他朋友的交易一结束就启程返回江苏江阴。但很快我们就被捕了。
此为实情。

我从未在政府职位、警察、军队等工作过。

签名：TSANG AH KYUNG。

File No.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
177/38
H. C. C. B. Start 6799/24
No. S. B. D. 38 / 2 / 38
Dec. 29, 1938
REPORT
Date December 29, 1938
Subject ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE
Made by D. S. Bradley Forwarded by D. I. Glover

Sir,

On 28-12-38, D.S.I. Umemoto attached to the
Special Political Office reported that Warrant Officer
Shimowatari of the Japanese Military Police had information
that a male Chinese had arrived in Shanghai from Chinkiang
to buy arms for guerille troops. The male Chinese could be
arrested at a certain hotel at 7 a.m. 29-12-38 and assistance
was requested to effect his arrest.

The necessary assistance was given by T.D.S. 304
and the undersigned and at 7.30 a.m. 29-12-38 a raid was
carried out on room 52 of the Ong Siang (鴻祥) Lodging House,
20 Avenue Road, where the following 5 male Chinese were
arrested as they were pointed out by the Japanese Military
Police as being suspected in attempting to buy arms :-

(1) TSANG ZAU LIH (張兆蘭), 25, Kiangyin, M/Un-employed, Kiangyin.
(2) LOH OEU ZAU (劉和尚), 32, Kiangyin, M/Farmer, Kiangyin.
(3) SUNG TAI KAU (孫斗閣), 36, Kiangyin, M/Tailor, Kiangyin.
(4) TSANG AH KYUNG (張阿琴), 33, Kiangyin, M/Boatman, Kiangyin.
(5) WONG CHING FONG (王金芳), 34, Kiangyin, M/Farmer, Kiangyin.

These men were questioned and they stated that
they were natives and residents of Kiangyin who had brought
204 bags of rice from Kiangyin to Shanghai to sell on 22-12-38.

They denied being in Shanghai to buy arms but the
Japanese Military Police state that the rice brought to Shanghai
by the 5 men was stolen and they intended to utilise the money
paid for it to buy arms.

1938 年 12 月 29 日
报告
日期 1938 年 12 月 29 日
事由：协助日本宪兵队
呈报人：D. S. Bradley 转呈人：D. I. Glover

先生，

1938 年 12 月 28 日，附属特别政治办公室的 D.S.I. Umemoto 报告称，日本宪兵队的 Shimowatari 准尉获悉，一名中国男子从镇江（Chinkiang）抵达上海，旨在为游击队购买武器。该中国男子可于 1938 年 12 月 29 日上午 7 时在一家特定旅馆被捕，并请求协助实施逮捕。

T.D.S. 304 和本人提供了必要的协助，并于 1938 年 12 月 29 日上午 7:30 对爱文义路（Avenue Road）20 号鸿祥（Ong Siang）旅馆的 52 号房间进行了突击搜查，在日本宪兵队指认下，以下 5 名中国男子因涉嫌企图购买武器而被捕：-

(1) TSANG ZAU LIH (張兆蘭)，25 岁，江苏江阴人，男/无业，江苏江阴。
(2) LOH OEU ZAU (劉和尚)，32 岁，江苏江阴人，男/农民，江苏江阴。
(3) SUNG TAI KAU (孫斗閣)，36 岁，江苏江阴人，男/裁缝，江苏江阴。
(4) TSANG AH KYUNG (張阿琴)，33 岁，江苏江阴人，男/船夫，江苏江阴。
(5) WONG CHING FONG (王金芳)，34 岁，江苏江阴人，男/农民，江苏江阴。

经讯问，这些人声称他们是江苏江阴的居民，于 1938 年 12 月 22 日从江苏江阴带了 204 袋大米到上海出售。

他们否认来上海是为了购买武器，但日本宪兵队称，这 5 人带到上海的大米是偷窃所得，他们打算利用出售大米所得的钱款购买武器。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No. ____

              - 2 -
Subject............................................................
Made by.................... Forwarded by.........................

The 5 accused deny that the rice was stolen and
the 3rd accused produced a bill of sale for the rice which he
brought to Shanghai.

The rice is at present stored in Shanhaikwan Road
and the persons storing same have been informed that the rice
should not be removed until further enquiries have been made.

The information given to C.B.H.Q. by D.S.I.
Umemoto does not seem to be very accurate, as it was alleged
that only one person from Chinkiang was to be arrested whilst
now the Japanese Military Police have arrested 5 men from
Kiangyin.

The Japanese Military Police request the immediate
handing over of the 5 accused, but they have been informed by
the undersigned that they will have to apply in the usual
manner for the 5 accused who are meanwhile being detained at
C.B.H.Q.

（批：HCS 27/12.）

                                        I am, Sir,
                                        Yours obediently,

                                        J Bradley

这 5 名被告否认大米是偷窃所得，第 3 名被告出示了他带到上海的大米的销售单据。

大米目前储存在山海关路，已通知储存者在进行进一步调查之前不得移动大米。

D.S.I. Umemoto 向总部刑事科（C.B.H.Q.）提供的情报似乎不太准确，因为据称只有一名来自镇江的人将被逮捕，而现在日本宪兵队逮捕了 5 名来自江苏江阴的人。

日本宪兵队要求立即移交这 5 名被告，但本人已告知他们，必须按常规程序申请移交这 5 名被告，他们目前正被拘押在总部刑事科（C.B.H.Q.）。

（批：HCS 27/12.）
